title: Traffic steering playbook and emergency hotfix for cross-region degradation
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Summary: Several customer escalations during a cross-region maintenance window revealed a bug in the traffic-steering logic used by Hosted and Dedicated routing layers. Symptoms included sustained elevated latency, 5xx tail errors for multi-region sessions, and failed KV cache reconciliations for Private deployments with region failover enabled. This ticket tracks the emergency hotfix, short-term operational playbook updates, and a handoff to the reliability squad for longer-term remediation.
updates: 2026-02-28 - 09:12 UTC: PagerDuty alert P384 triggered for cross-region latency spike after region maintenance start. Notified oncall SRE (Rohit Patel).

2026-02-28 - 09:30 UTC: Initial triage: routing service returned inconsistent backend candidate lists when a region reported partial capacity. Observed mixing of v2 and fallback routing policies. Impacting hosted API customers and several Dedicated pools.

2026-02-28 - 10:05 UTC: Rolled an emergency toggle to force 'region-strict' policy for affected customers to prevent cross-region lane mixing. Immediate latency improvement for most sessions. Documented temporary toggle in incident chronicle: https://redwood.atlassian.net/incident/P384
2026-02-28 - 11:40 UTC: Customer escalations from two enterprise customers (Acme AI, Callisto Health). Opened support threads and scheduled live bridge. Provided status and mitigation steps.

2026-02-28 - 14:20 UTC: Deployed hotfix patch (routing-service#PR-742) that adds atomic policy upgrade and guards against mixed-policy reads under partial cluster view. Patch PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing-service/pull/742

2026-02-28 - 15:05 UTC: Hotfix rolled to canary, smoke tests passed (latency and 5xx at normal levels). Gradual rollout to remaining regions completed by 15:50 UTC. Observability: reduced 99th percentile by ~320ms. Grafana dashboard: https://grafana.redwood-internal/boards/region-steering

2026-02-29 - 09:00 UTC: Private deployments: discovered KV cache reconciliation failures when clients were moved to fallback pools. Short-term workaround applied: clear stale prefix caches on failover and trigger async reconciliation. Added script: https://github.com/redwood-inference/tools/commit/4f2d9

2026-03-03 - 12:00 UTC: Post-deploy customer follow-ups complete. Customers accepted mitigation but requested a formal playbook and API-level promise for traffic shifting. Added request to project backlog.

2026-03-05 - 10:30 UTC: Design decision: Introduce explicit traffic-shift phases (prepare -> drain -> cutover -> validate) in the routing control plane rather than immediate atomic swaps. This reduces cache mismatch windows but increases shift latency by ~200ms in worst case. Recorded trade-off and sign-off from PM (Lena Kim).

2026-03-08 - 16:00 UTC: Drafted operational playbook and run-validation checklist. Shared with SRE, Platform, and Solutions Eng for review. Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/RDEV/pages/Traffic+Steering+Playbook
2026-03-10 - 11:15 UTC: Added unit + e2e tests around mixed-policy reads/writes and KV reconciliation. Tests are green on CI. Preparing rollout plan for runtime-1.24.
next_steps: Finalize playbook language and add explicit step-by-step commands for oncall (clear TTLs, toggle policy, validate sessions)
Ship runtime-1.24 containing phased traffic-shift control plane and KV reconciliation fix (target: 2026-03-17)
Create a dedicated e2e harness to simulate region flaps and validate traffic-shift phases under load
Introduce API flags for customers to choose 'strict-region' vs 'latency-first' steering modes at account level
acceptance_criteria: All new unit and e2e tests green in CI for routing and kv reconciliation
Playbook accepted by SRE and Solutions Eng and published in Confluence
runtime-1.24 rollout completed to 100% with no regressions for 72 hours
Support runbooks updated and a post-deployment verification check added to deployment pipelines
